newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares open weaker on autumn unease, franc.
newsitem.headline: French shares open weaker on autumn unease, franc.

text.p: French shares opened slightly weaker for the second day running on Tuesday amid growing unease about a difficult autumn for the government which also weighed on the franc, dealers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index opened down 5.69 points or 0.28 percent at 2,014.73 after dipping 0.02 percent on Monday.

Bond prices were weaker and the franc was quoted at 3.4210 francs per mark for the first time since August 13 as worries about the government's autumn budget and a weak U.S. currency lifted the mark and squeezed French investments.
The franc was nearly half a centime weaker compared with late Monday's European levels at 3.4205 per mark and the 10-year bond future contract was slightly easier.
Construction company SGE fell 5.7 percent in early dealings to 97 francs after rising 7.8 percent on Monday on rumours that parent Cie Generale des Eaux would buy out minorities.

Opthalmic products manufacturer Essilor rose 0.4 percent to 1,300 francs after Oakley Inc of the United States said it had been granted an option to buy the non-prescription lens production unit of Gentext Optics Inc, an Essilor subsidiary.
The majority of leading shares was weaker, however, with industrial giant Alcatel Alsthom, a heavyweight on the share index, retreating 1.4 percent to 396.2 francs.

Later on Tuesday the countdown starts to what investors fear could be a fretful autumn for the government and financial markets, with unions threatening protests against a planned government spending freeze for 1997.

France's main teachers unions meet to discuss government plans to axe round 7,000 civil service jobs which are seen likely to include education posts. Two teaching unions have already called strike action for late September.
Dealers said they were looking for an improvement in share volume after Monday's flat turnover of 1.6 billion francs, depressed by London's absence for a public holiday.
But barring upsets, analysts said technical charts pointed to a narrow 20-point trading range between 2,008 and 2,028 points on the CAC-40 index for the time being.
